in_hebrew.name: יתן
in_hebrew.meaning: הענקת אלוהים, נתינת אלוהים, יש תוכנית אלוהית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יתן מגיע מהשורש העברי 'נתן', שפירושו לתת או להעניק. בהקשר של שמות פרטיים, הוא מתפרש כמתנת אלוהים או להעניק מאלוהים. השם מופיע בתנ"ך ככינויו של אחד מנשיאי שבט יהודה, וגם כשם של כמה דמויות מקראיות אחרות.

in_greek.name: Ιηθαν
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ιηθαν είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος העברי 'יתן' (Yethan), που σημαίνει 'Θεός δίδει' (ο Θεός δίνει) ή 'Δοσθενος' (δοσθενος). Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόλο που δεν αναφέρεται συγκεκριμένα, οι ερμηνείες των ονομάτων συνδέονται συχνά με θεολογική σημασία.

in_latin.name: Jethan
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Jethan derivatur ex radice hebraica 'נתן' (nathan), quae donare significat. In contextu nominum propria, interpretatur ut 'donum Dei' vel 'donatio Dei'. Nomen in Biblia Hebraica invenitur ut nomen unius e principibus tribus Iudae.

in_english.name: Jethan
in_english.meaning: Gift of God, God's gift, God gives
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jethan originates from the Hebrew root 'נתן' (nathan), meaning 'to give'. It is interpreted as 'God's gift' or 'gift of God'. In the Bible, Jethan is mentioned as a leader of the tribe of Judah. The name carries spiritual significance as a reminder of divine providence and blessing. It symbolizes a child being a precious gift from God.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jethro appears in the Old Testament and is of Hebrew origin. It was the name of Moses' father-in-law and the priest of Midian, displaying the influence of ancient Middle Eastern cultures on religious names. (approximately 1-2 sentences)
data.spiritual_significance: Jethan, a derivative of the Hebrew name Yehudah, means 'God will add'. This is a reflection of the belief in God's role in amplifying the strength and blessings of an individual. (approximately 1-2 sentences)
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jethan, meaning "God's gift," highlights the belief that every individual is a divine present bestowed upon the world by the Creator. This name serves as a constant reminder of the divine origin and purpose of human existence.

biblical_reference.note: Jethan is mentioned as one of the descendants of Judah.

historical_references.reference: Saint Jethro, also known as Ethan the Aethiopian or the Moabite, was a biblical prophet and priest who converted King David to Judaism. This event occurred around 1000 BCE during the early monarchy period in Israel.

Ethan the Scribe was a poet and musician mentioned in the Old Testament Book of Psalms. Ethan was one of the musicians who accompanied King David during his reign, around 1000-550 BCE. He is credited with writing several psalms.

modern_usage.modern_context: Jethan is a character from Hebrew mythology who is most commonly known as the high priest of Midian and the father of Moses' wife Zipporah. In modern contexts, Jethro's name is seen on various platforms as a character of interest in discussions related to mythology, fantasy literature, and role-playing games. On Reddit, users may create threads discussing Jethro's role in the Bible or compare him to other mythological figures. On Goodreads, there may be books about Jethro or his role in the Bible, which users can review and discuss. On D&D Beyond, Jethro may be used as a background or a custom character in Dungeons & Dragons games.
